    AI Overview
    A criminal defense attorney
    provides legal representation to individuals accused of crimes, navigating state or federal courts to protect their rights and secure the best outcome, such as a plea bargain, acquittal, or reduced sentencing. They manage tasks like investigating cases, interviewing witnesses, gathering evidence, and filing motions. 
    Key aspects of a criminal attorney's role include: 
    • Representation: Representing individuals in misdemeanor and felony cases, including DUIs, drug crimes, violent crimes, and theft.
    • Defense Strategy: Researching legal precedents, evaluating the prosecution's case, and developing defense strategies.
    • Court Advocacy:
      Appearing in court hearings on behalf of clients and negotiating with prosecutors.
    • Investigation: Gathering evidence and finding expert witnesses to support the defense. 
    Key Considerations 
    • Experience & Specialization: Choosing an attorney with specific experience in criminal defense—particularly one familiar with local courts—is often more effective than a general practitioner.
    • Former Prosecutors: Some defense attorneys are former prosecutors, which can provide insight into how cases are built against them.
    • When to Hire: It is crucial to hire a lawyer immediately, especially if under investigation or if a warrant has been issued.
    • Process: The process often begins with a free consultation and evaluation, where they assess the case and advise on the next steps. 
    Legal Roles & Responsibilities
    Criminal attorneys ensure that the rights of the accused are not violated, such as protecting them from illegal searches and seizures, or ensuring proper procedures are followed. Their goal is to navigate the legal system to minimize penalties, such as jail time or fines.
